bullets.title: GS flow desk: HFs net selling tech/comms at 98th-pct; hyperscalers vs semis rotation
bullets.body: Goldman's floor reported -5.5% better-for-sale overall, with hedge funds -15% better-for-sale in a move that ranks in the 98th percentile over the past year. The firm flagged a clear rotation theme: buying hyperscalers (Mag7 outperforming NDX by ~3%) while selling semis/memory (GSPRHIMO basket -6.5% on the day). Long-only accounts were slightly better to buy.

bullets.title: NVDA: Jensen denies Vera Rubin delay; says production already underway 'in giant amounts'
bullets.body: From Tokyo, Jensen Huang stated directly that reports of AI server manufacturing delays are 'not true' and that Vera Rubin is already in production with large shipment volumes coming. Separately, millions of dollars in NVDA put sweepers were detected intraday, suggesting some downside hedging despite the CEO denial.

bullets.title: NVDA/NOK: Launch first AI-RAN platform; 20%+ spectral efficiency gains, subscription model
bullets.body: Nokia and Nvidia announced the first AI-RAN platform delivering over 20% spectral efficiency gains initially, targeting 50% by 2027 and 100%+ by 2028. The product is sold as a software subscription rather than hardware, potentially opening a recurring revenue stream for both companies.

bullets.title: AMD: Helios rack shipments reportedly delayed out of 2026 despite company denial
bullets.body: A source claims visibility that AMD Helios rack shipments are delayed beyond this year, contradicting AMD's public denial of any delays. The source expresses confidence in their read despite the pushback.

bullets.title: DELL: Extends drop to 13%, worst since April 2025
bullets.body: Dell shares fell as much as 13% intraday, the largest single-day decline since April 2025, dropping from $460 to $405 in under two hours. No specific catalyst cited in the flow, though the move tracked broader semi/storage sector weakness.

bullets.title: SNDK: Drops 11% to session low; DRAM 20%+ price hike expected next quarter despite selloff
bullets.body: SanDisk extended losses to a session-low -11%. Separately, a source flagged that DRAM prices are expected to increase 20%+ next quarter, SNDK is securing long-term agreements with META and MU, and laser supplies are sold out into early 2029—suggesting the selloff is disconnecting from strong underlying fundamentals.

bullets.title: MU: Conflicting signals — call sweepers bullish but sell-side warns on DRAM price resistance
bullets.body: Large MU call sweepers were observed again (millions in notional), and one trader recommended buying at $885 with multi-month conviction. However, GFHK lowered its Q3 DRAM price growth forecasts citing customer pushback near 30% hikes, while a separate trader recommended taking profits on MU. Memory sector broadly sold despite bullish fundamental backdrop.

bullets.title: AAPL: Hits ATH; pursuing AI chip acquisitions per The Information; M2 Ultra underperforms on AI
bullets.body: Apple hit new all-time highs intraday and is within $250B of a $5T market cap. The Information reports Apple is approaching chip startups to gauge acquisition interest, aiming to build server chips for AI. Separately, M2 Ultra chips reportedly fell short for advanced AI workloads, forcing Apple to rely on Nvidia for compute needs. Alibaba's Qwen AI is also set to be integrated into Apple Intelligence for China, sending BABA up 5.7%.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Up 3%+ intraday; withdraws Epic antitrust appeal; permits third-party app stores
bullets.body: Google shares gained over 3% on the day. The company pulled its request to change the court ruling in the Epic antitrust case and separately announced it will permit third-party app stores in its Play Store starting next week — a significant regulatory compliance move.

bullets.title: META: $12M OTM call sweep detected; market cap now exceeds MSFT by 28%
bullets.body: A trader placed $12M in OTM META calls expiring in two months, signaling speculative upside positioning. Meta's market cap now surpasses both Saudi Aramco and Microsoft (larger than MSFT by ~28%), reflecting strong year-to-date performance.

bullets.title: UBER: Nearing €12.5B deal to acquire Delivery Hero; announcement expected Thursday
bullets.body: Uber is in advanced negotiations to acquire Delivery Hero for approximately €12.5 billion, with an announcement expected as early as Thursday. As part of the deal, Delivery Hero would divest its Turkish unit Yemeksepeti and several European businesses to an investment firm.

bullets.title: INTC: Trading below $100; High NA EUV with 14A seen as scale option for customers
bullets.body: Intel shares broke below the $100 level intraday. On the product side, analysis of ASML's Q&A session highlighted Intel as potentially helping clean the pipe for High NA EUV, with 14A emerging as a possible scale option for chipmaking customers.

bullets.title: COHR/LITE: Optical stocks 'completely sold'; Rosenblatt channel check flags sector weakness
bullets.body: Rosenblatt channel checks flagged weakness in the optical sector impacting networking equipment vendors including COHR and LITE. A trader noted these names are 'completely sold' but sees no fundamental problems, characterizing the correction as leverage-flushing ahead of a resumption higher.

bullets.title: WBD/PSKY: Paramount's legal tactics signal weak trial confidence despite public bravado
bullets.body: LightShed notes Paramount's lead trial counsel hinted the case could go to the Supreme Court and hired prominent appellate lawyer Paul Clement — signals the analyst interprets as weak trial prospects rather than confidence. Paramount is also threatening to leave California and name-checking Netflix in filings, contradicting its 'slam dunk' characterization of the WBD deal.

bullets.title: EQIX: Trump files purchase order up to $1M; cites data centers as biggest future jobs driver
bullets.body: Trump filed a purchase order for up to $1,000,000 of EQIX stock and stated on Truth Social that data centers are 'one of the biggest driving forces in the future for jobs.' He also criticized NY Governor Hochul for terminating data center projects in the state.

bullets.title: DIS: FCC nearing rulings against Disney over 'The View' and TV licenses
bullets.body: The FCC is reportedly close to issuing adverse rulings against Disney related to 'The View' programming and Disney's TV licenses, representing a potential regulatory headwind for the media giant.

bullets.title: MSFT: Microsoft and 3M announce AI data center infrastructure partnership
bullets.body: Microsoft and 3M entered into a new strategic partnership focused on AI data center infrastructure and enterprise transformation. MSFT is also developing its own internal AI models alongside external partnerships.

bullets.title: Semi sector: SMH -3.7% intraday; semis haven't dropped >2% on a Nasdaq-up day since Nov 2024
bullets.body: The SMH semiconductor ETF fell 3.7% from the open despite indices starting higher, extending an unusual run of volatility. A technical note flags that semis have not been down more than 2% on any day when the Nasdaq finished higher since November 2024 — making today's action historically notable.

bullets.title: Macro: PPI -0.3% MoM (est. 0.0%), YoY +5.5% vs +6.2% est.; July rate hike odds collapse
bullets.body: June PPI came in sharply below expectations at -0.3% MoM and +5.5% YoY (vs. +6.2% est.), following yesterday's soft CPI. The miss is large enough that market pricing for a July rate hike was effectively eliminated, though Fed Governor Cook signaled she needs to see disinflation materialize 'soon' before cutting and Warsh flagged ongoing inflation concerns. NY Empire State Manufacturing also beat at +15.6 vs. +9.2 est.

bullets.title: IREN: Appoints Eric Hammersley as Chief Information Security Officer
bullets.body: IREN appointed Eric Hammersley as its new CISO to lead the company's security program. No financial guidance changes were disclosed alongside the announcement.
